name: Token risk check on 30 labelled mints
threshold: blocks 9/9 seizure mints (a permanent delegate or a live transfer hook, either of which can take or immobilise the position), 0/11 blue chips, and 0/10 fee-only Token-2022 mints, which are reported with their basis points rather than blocked; a freeze authority is reported with its own reason and never blocks on its own

supersedes.threshold: flags 20/20 dangerous mints (10 with live freeze or mint authority, 10 Token-2022 with permanent delegate, transfer hook or transfer fee) and 0/10 blue chips
supersedes.measured: 10/20 dangerous flagged, 2/10 blue chips flagged (USDC, USDT)
supersedes.why: The old threshold contradicted itself. It labelled a set dangerous for carrying a live freeze authority while requiring 0 blue chips flagged, and USDC and USDT both have one, as do PYUSD, USDG, cbBTC and the tokenised equities. One rule cannot call that trait disqualifying and wave the two largest stablecoins on Solana through. For a regulated issuer a freeze authority is how a court order is obeyed; for a memecoin deployer it is how your position is taken, and the mint account cannot tell those apart. It also grouped a transfer fee, which is a cost, with a permanent delegate, which is a seizure. The new threshold says what the guard blocks on. Telling Circle from a stranger needs an issuer allowlist, which is T-C06 work with a threshold of its own.
supersedes.relabelled: cbBTC moved from the seizure set to blue chip. It was the only mint there with no permanent delegate, and it is Coinbase's wrapped BTC.

notes: Copied from T-C11's Acceptance line before the re-run. The 30 mints are labelled in mints.json, and the recorded response sits in recorded/ beside them so the two cannot drift. Directory is spikes/F3 and not spikes/F03 because scripts/spike.mjs resolves spikes/${id}/run.mjs from the id in spike:f3.
